cynical

SIN-ih-kul — a cynical person assumes everyone has a hidden, selfish motive. · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Cynical is distrustful of the motives of others; believing people are mainly driven by self-interest.

After years of broken promises from politicians, she became deeply cynical about every campaign speech she heard.

Example

A charity announces it raised a record amount of donations this year. Instead of feeling encouraged, a cynical longtime critic immediately assumes the organization must be exaggerating the number just to attract even more donors next year.

He automatically assumes a hidden, selfish motive behind the good news. Unlike 'careful,' which is simply cautious, cynical specifically means distrusting people's true intentions.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

distrustful: Distrustful means not trusting — suspicious of a particular person or claim. Cynical goes further and wider: a cynical person assumes from the start that people in general are driven by self-interest, before anyone has given a specific reason for doubt.

wary: Wary means cautious and on guard because something might go wrong — you can be wary of ice on the steps. Cynical is a settled attitude about people: it assumes their motives are selfish, while wariness is careful alertness that passes when the danger does.

pessimistic: Pessimistic means expecting the worst outcome — the plan will fail, the rain will come. Cynical is not about outcomes but about motives: a cynical person may think a plan will succeed while still assuming everyone behind it is in it for themselves.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

trusting: believing in the honesty and good intentions of others

idealistic: believing in the best possible outcome or in noble motives

Where it sits · how deeply trust has worn away — skeptical → cynical → jaded

skeptical vs. cynical: Skeptical is a milder word than cynical — being skeptical just means you want proof before believing something, while cynical assumes people's motives are selfish from the start.

jaded vs. cynical: Jaded can feel even more worn down than cynical: cynical is a general distrust of motives, but jaded specifically comes from being disappointed so many times that nothing excites you anymore.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — cyn-/kyn-

root — cyn-/kyn-: dog (Greek (kyon))

Put it together

Put it together: Cynical traces back to the ancient Greek Cynic philosophers, whose name came from kyon, 'dog' -- possibly because they lived simply and rejected social conventions the way a stray dog ignores manners. Over centuries, 'cynic' drifted from that philosophy toward today's meaning: distrusting people's true motives.

Use the root in a new word: cynosure

Use the root in a new word: cynosure: The young actress quickly became the cynosure of the entire room.
